extracted.subtask_description: Crafting short news articles reporting fires, accidents, shipwrecks, mine explosions and drownings, using standard news-lede structure, source attribution, survivor quotes, and human-interest detail. Examples show variations in arrangement and emphasis across wire services and papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification by beat (Fires and Accidents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are organized under the beat/category 'Fires and Accidents'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the beat label to group related incidents (shipwrecks, mine explosions, drownings, falls, scaffolding accidents, etc.), signaling to readers the general topic and expected content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different arrangements of the same material
rubrics_metrics.description: The same facts can be arranged in different ways by different news associations, producing distinct versions of the same incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes explicitly: 'The following two stories illustrate different arrangements of the same material and were probably telegraphed by different news associations.' Compare versions to see how emphasis, order, and selection differ; choose arrangement that foregrounds the most newsworthy element for your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with the most newsworthy fact (fatalities, rescue, disaster magnitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open with the central fact — number killed or rescued, scale of disaster, or immediate dramatic action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Between seventy and eighty men, women, and children... were drowned' (lede for the Leggett shipwreck); 'Within three minutes ... the model Marianna mine ... was blown up' (mine explosion). Place casualty counts or dramatic action in the opening paragraph to orient the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include precise factual details (who, what, when, where, how, vessel/specifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete specifics: names, locations, dates/times, vessel tonnage/dimensions, numbers of persons, distances, and other technical particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples throughout: ship gross register and dimensions, exact distances from buoys, number of tons of coal, number of victims (e.g., 275), time of explosion (11:30). These details lend authority and allow readers to understand scale and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use attributed eyewitness and survivor accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate first-person or eyewitness reports and attribute them by name or role to give immediacy and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: survivor Alexander Farrell's account of lifeboats capsizing; quotes and reported actions of Capt. Jensen, Capt. Moro, and rescuers. Attribute quotes and recollections to named individuals or identified roles (survivor, captain, witness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution and dateline/header conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate the originating paper or wire (e.g., 'Philadelphia Ledger', 'New York Times') and use datelines (city, date) for location and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each example carries a source credit and dateline (e.g., 'ASTORIA, Ore., Sept. 19.—') or a paper header. Maintain these conventions to show provenance, especially when combining or comparing versions from different services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest detail and scene-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Include emotive or scene-setting details (families, survivors' condition, crowds, behavior of rescuers) to give readers a human sense of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: descriptions of grieving crowds at the mine, Mrs. Stock and her children after the baby drowned, exhausted crews working pumps. Use such details to create pathos and contextualize the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain ongoing investigations and official responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the status of official inquiries, investigations, and responses (inspectors, company officials, mine-testing stations) and note when responsibility is undetermined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'An investigation to determine this will be made by the United States Steamboat Inspectors.' and accounts of mine inspectors and company officials rushing to the scene. Report what authorities say and what steps are being taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe rescue efforts and methods used
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail rescue operations, techniques, equipment, and difficulties encountered in saving victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: pumps manned in shifts, rescuers burrowing at the mouth of the mine, use of patented helmets, transfer of survivors between ships. Such detail explains the challenges and valor of rescuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note uncertainties and variations in early reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge uncertain or varying early figures, ailments, or causes when information is incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: varying initial casualty counts, 'Whether the gas... was communicated to the mine... cannot now be ascertained', and differences between wire-service versions. Signal uncertainty and update as facts are confirmed.
